12:00 Local Time, 07:00 GMT, 12:30 IST: Hello and welcome, everyone! Pakistan and Sri Lanka lock horns after pulling off two remarkable, almost improbable wins over England in their respective last outings. Sri Lanka were the first to do the unthinkable, chasing down a mammoth target of 430 last Thursday. Then, on Sunday, Pakistan looked down and out at 154/9 while chasing 242, only for Shadab Khan to produce the kind of innings you dream of playing as a kid. He brought up his maiden international hundred and stitched together an unbeaten 89-run stand for the last wicket to pull off a miraculous victory. Pakistan have won all three of their games so far and have already booked their place in the final. Sri Lanka, meanwhile, have two matches left, including this one, and a win today would see them join Pakistan in the summit clash, rendering their final league game against England a dead rubber.

The Men in Green may be unbeaten, but they have their fair share of concerns, with the top order being the biggest of them all. Saim Ayub, Fakhar Zaman and Babar Azam have managed a combined average of just over 15 in this series. Ayub has already been released from the squad and replaced by Sahibzada Farhan, while Maaz Sadaqat could also come into the XI. Then there is Babar, who has averaged in the mid-30s since 2025 and has often thrown away promising starts. His strike rate of 74.31 over this period is another major concern.

Sri Lanka, meanwhile, will want more from their captain, Kusal Mendis, who is yet to make a significant contribution with the bat in this series. Their bowling has also been below par, and the inclusion of someone like Maheesh Theekshana could give them better control. Unlike the surface in Rawalpindi, where Sri Lanka pulled off that remarkable chase, the Lahore pitch is slightly slower, as seen in the last game between Pakistan and England. Sri Lanka will be keen to get the job done tonight rather than leave their fate hanging on the final league game against England. A win would seal their place in the final, so there is plenty at stake. Stay tuned as we bring you the toss and team news shortly...

Kusal Mendis: We are going to bowl first. [Why's that] I think a little bit dew is coming in the second innings. That's the first reason. And I trust our batting unit. The guys batted really well in last game. [On chasing 430 vs England] I think we did (some) really good partnerships, and we did the process, and Janith (Liyanage), Pavan Rathnayake, Dasun (Shanaka), Avishka (Fernando), they batted really well. Then we enjoyed a lot in the dressing room, I'm very happy. [On the playing XI] We (are) going to same combination because the guys bowled really well in the powerplay. I'm very happy (with the) bowling unit.

Shaheen Afridi: We would have also bowled first because in the second half, there's a little bit dew. [On the last game vs England] Amazing game. Never seen a game like that. A good sign for Pakistan. You know, any player can come and win the game for us, which is good. [What kind of score do you think is defendable on this surface?] I feel like 290-300, and then the kind of bowling we have, so we (would be) comfortable with that. [Any changes] We have two changes. Pitch Report | Aamer Sohail: It looks a belter. It's rock hard with a lot of grass covering, and I think it'll offer consistent pace and bounce. However, initially, initially for a few overs, just for a few overs, it might offer a bit of grip. Other than that, in my opinion, this pitch should behave.

Haris Rauf (Translated to English) 1/3: [On his match-winning last-wicket stand with Shadab Khan against England] At that time, given the situation, I just told him to believe in me because anything could happen. It's cricket, and he needed to trust me. As a tail-ender, batters usually have less trust in you, but my conversation with him was that he should believe in me and trust me. My temperament was very important at that point. I had to control my nerves and stay calm because I couldn't just start hitting. The partner at the other end has his own role, and until he gives you the chance, you need to show a lot of temperament. You have to control your nerves and remain calm. It wasn't easy, but he guided me a lot, which helped. I also guided him during those three or four balls when he was playing a little loosely. After that, I went to him and said, "Stay a little tighter. I feel your body language is getting a bit loose." He agreed and said, "Absolutely, I'll be a little tighter on the next ball."

Rauf 3/3: [You bowl with both new and old balls. Which role suits you best?] Throughout my career, I've bowled as the first change from the very beginning. When a new bowler wasn't available, or someone was injured or struggling, I had to take on that role in every match, whatever the situation. As a player and a bowler, you accept challenges rather than saying, "I don't bowl with the new ball, so why should I?" That's not how you work as a professional. Personally, I want to be at the forefront whenever the Pakistan team needs me. I want to accept those challenges and try to improve in that role for Pakistan.
Ehsan Sabir: I think in this Pakistan side, everyone wants to win games for the team. Everyone shows great temperament and supports each other, which is very good for the team.
